title: Rate of Convergence for Orthonormal Expansions (Fourier, Legendre)
description: For an orthonormal family v in an inner product space, the orthonormal partial sum S s = ∑ i ∈ s, ⟪vᵢ,x⟫ • vᵢ is the orthogonal projection of x onto the span of {vᵢ : i ∈ s} — the abstract Fourier/Legendre partial sum. The parent (cauchy-schwarz-oq-02-oq-02) records Bessel's inequality ∑' i, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ‖x‖². This entry studies the RATE at which S s converges to x. Mathlib proves the exact error identity ‖x − S s‖² = ‖x‖² − ∑ i ∈ s, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² INSIDE its Bessel proof but never exports it; we extract it (norm_sub_partialSum_sq) and build the quantitative theory: the squared error is monotone non-increasing, converges to the Parseval defect ‖x‖² − ∑' ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖², vanishes iff Parseval holds, and — under Parseval with geometric coefficient decay ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ C rⁱ (the analytic/smooth regime of Fourier and Legendre series) — obeys the explicit geometric rate ‖x − S(range n)‖² ≤ C rⁿ/(1−r). 7 theorems, 1 def, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Lean Genius

mathlibDependencies.description: The double-sum collapse ∑∑ ⟪vᵢ,x⟫⟪x,vⱼ⟫⟪vⱼ,vᵢ⟫ = ∑ ⟪vₖ,x⟫⟪x,vₖ⟫ for an orthonormal family — the algebraic core of the error identity
Summability of i ↦ ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² (from Bessel's inequality), giving the convergence of the partial Bessel sums
(∑ i ∈ range n, f i) + ∑' i, f (i + n) = ∑' i, f i — splits a series into a finite head and its tail, identifying the post-n error with the coefficient tail
Summability and value (1−r)⁻¹ of the geometric series ∑' rⁿ for 0 ≤ r < 1 — the quantitative engine of the geometric rate
Termwise domination ∀ i, f i ≤ g i lifts to ∑' f ≤ ∑' g (both summable) — bounds the coefficient tail by the geometric tail
Uniqueness of limits in a Hausdorff space — turns convergence of the squared error to 0 into the Parseval identity

originalContributions: norm_sub_partialSum_sq: the EXACT error identity ‖x − S s‖² = ‖x‖² − ∑ i ∈ s, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖², extracted as a standalone reusable lemma. Mathlib proves precisely this as an unnamed `suffices` step inside Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le but never exposes it; it is the engine of all convergence-rate analysis.

sq_error_antitone: the squared approximation error is monotone non-increasing in the index set — enlarging s never worsens the approximation, decreasing the error by exactly the squared coefficients of the added basis vectors.
partialSum_isBestApprox_le: Bessel's finite inequality ∑ i ∈ s, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ‖x‖² recovered as a one-line corollary of the error identity and norm-nonnegativity.
tendsto_sq_error: the squared error converges, along the directed set of finite index sets, to the Parseval defect ‖x‖² − ∑' i, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖².
tendsto_partialSum_iff_parseval: the partial sums converge to x (in norm) IFF Parseval's identity ∑' i, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² = ‖x‖² holds — completeness of the orthonormal system at x.
sq_error_eq_tail_of_parseval: under Parseval, the squared error after n terms equals the tail ∑' k, ‖⟪v(k+n),x⟫‖² — the exact object a rate bounds.

geometric_rate: under Parseval with geometric coefficient decay ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ C rⁱ (0 ≤ r < 1), the explicit geometric convergence rate ‖x − S(range n)‖² ≤ C rⁿ/(1−r) — the Fourier/Legendre behaviour for analytic/smooth functions.
meta.assumptions: None. All 7 theorems fully proved with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (no native_decide); #print axioms reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Results hold for an orthonormal family v : ι → E over any RCLike field 𝕜 (ℝ or ℂ) in any inner product space E; the geometric-rate results specialize the index to ℕ and assume Parseval at x (i.e. completeness, as holds for a Hilbert basis / complete orthonormal system) plus a geometric decay bound on the coefficients. No assumption is encoded in any structure beyond Mathlib's Orthonormal predicate.

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: Bessel's inequality in infinite dimensions (∑' ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ ‖x‖² and summability). This entry builds on the summability it provides to quantify the convergence rate of the orthonormal partial sums.

overview.historicalContext: Expanding a function in an orthonormal system — trigonometric (Fourier), Legendre, Hermite, wavelet — is the workhorse of analysis and numerical computation. The partial sum Sₙ = ∑_{i<n} ⟪vᵢ,x⟫ vᵢ is the best approximation of x from the first n basis vectors, and the central practical question is how fast Sₙ → x. Bessel's inequality guarantees the coefficients are square-summable, and Parseval's identity characterizes when the expansion is complete (Sₙ → x). The rate of convergence, however, is governed by the decay of the coefficients ⟪vᵢ,x⟫, which in turn reflects the smoothness of x: smoother functions have faster-decaying Fourier/Legendre coefficients and hence faster-converging expansions. Analytic functions enjoy geometric (exponential) coefficient decay and correspondingly geometric convergence — the regime captured here.
overview.problemStatement: For an orthonormal family v : ι → E and x ∈ E, with orthonormal partial sum S s = ∑ i ∈ s, ⟪vᵢ,x⟫ • vᵢ: (1) prove the exact error identity ‖x − S s‖² = ‖x‖² − ∑ i ∈ s, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖²; (2) show the squared error is monotone non-increasing and converges to the Parseval defect; (3) show convergence to x is equivalent to Parseval's identity; and (4) for ℕ-indexed families with geometric coefficient decay ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ C rⁱ under Parseval, derive the explicit geometric rate ‖x − S(range n)‖² ≤ C rⁿ/(1−r).
overview.proofStrategy: The keystone is the error identity, which Mathlib establishes inside its Bessel proof via the orthonormality collapse Orthonormal.inner_left_right_finset and norm_sub_sq; we extract it as norm_sub_partialSum_sq. Monotonicity is then immediate: enlarging the index set only adds non-negative terms to the subtracted Bessel sum (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg). Bessel's finite inequality follows from norm-nonnegativity. For convergence, Orthonormal.inner_products_summable gives HasSum of the squared coefficients, i.e. the partial Bessel sums tend to the tsum along the finite-subsets filter; subtracting from the constant ‖x‖² yields tendsto_sq_error, and uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique) gives the Parseval characterization. For the geometric rate, Summable.sum_add_tsum_nat_add identifies the post-n error with the coefficient tail; termwise domination (Summable.tsum_le_tsum) by C rⁱ and the closed form of the geometric series (tsum_geometric_of_lt_one) deliver the bound C rⁿ/(1−r).
keyInsights: The whole theory rests on one identity Mathlib hides: ‖x − S s‖² = ‖x‖² − ∑ i ∈ s, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖². Exposing it turns convergence-rate questions into elementary statements about the partial sums of the (non-negative) Bessel series.

Monotone improvement is structural: because every term ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² is non-negative, adding basis vectors can only shrink the error — the orthonormal partial sum is a genuine best approximation that never regresses.
Convergence of Sₙ to x is exactly Parseval's identity; the 'Parseval defect' ‖x‖² − ∑' ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² is the irreducible squared error, the squared distance from x to the closed span of the system.
Under completeness, the post-n error is literally the tail of the coefficient series; the convergence rate is therefore inherited verbatim from the decay rate of the coefficients.
Geometric coefficient decay ⇒ geometric convergence: ‖x − S(range n)‖² ≤ C rⁿ/(1−r). This is the abstract reason analytic functions have exponentially convergent Fourier and Legendre expansions.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 191 lines, 7 theorems and 1 definition developing the convergence-rate theory of orthonormal expansions. It extracts the error identity ‖x − S s‖² = ‖x‖² − ∑ i ∈ s, ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² that Mathlib proves but hides, then derives monotone improvement, convergence to the Parseval defect, the convergence ⟺ Parseval characterization, and an explicit geometric convergence rate ‖x − S(range n)‖² ≤ C rⁿ/(1−r) under geometric coefficient decay.
conclusion.implications: The standalone error identity is broadly reusable for any best-approximation or projection argument in inner product spaces. The geometric rate makes precise the classical heuristic 'smoother functions have faster-converging Fourier/Legendre series': geometric (exponential) coefficient decay — characteristic of analytic functions — yields geometric convergence of the partial sums. The development sits directly atop the parent's Bessel inequality, turning a qualitative summability statement into quantitative rates.
openQuestions: Derive algebraic rates ‖x − S(range n)‖² = O(n^{-α}) from polynomial coefficient decay ‖⟪vᵢ,x⟫‖² ≤ C i^{-(α+1)}, the Sobolev-smoothness regime, complementing the geometric (analytic-smoothness) case.
Specialize to the concrete Fourier and Legendre bases and connect coefficient decay to quantitative smoothness (Cᵏ / analyticity) of the expanded function.
Formalize the best-approximation optimality ‖x − S s‖ ≤ ‖x − ∑ i ∈ s, c i • vᵢ‖ for arbitrary coefficients c, exhibiting S s as the metric projection onto the finite span.
